To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Munc18‐ 2 is required for the localization of Syntaxin 11 to the plasma membane in cytotoxic T‐lyphocytes.
Munc18‐ 2 and STX 11 localize to different compartments within the cell, with Munc18‐‐2 localizing to cytolytic vesicles, while STX11 localizes predominantly to the plasma membrane.
Munc18‐ 2 is required for STX11 localization to the plasma membrane in CTL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the immune system works, and in this case how cytotoxic T‐lymphtocytes kill their targets.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate the exocytosis of secretory vesicles in cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL) and the consequences of defects in these mechanisms for the immune system.
the regulation of exocytosis and membrane fusion in immune cells, and how defects in these pathways can lead to human disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Munc18-2 is required for STX11 localization on the plasma membrane, where the final fusion event occurs.
Munc18‐ 2 is required for STX11 localization on the plasma membrane in cytotoxic T‐lympocytes.
Munc18‐1 is the main Munc18 protein involved in exocytosis in neuroendocrine cells, while Munc 18‐2 is the main Muc18 protein involved in CTL cytotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Munc18‐1 and Munc18-2 are required for the formation of the secretory apparatus in CTL.
STX11 and its chaperone, Munc18-2, are localized to the plasma membrane in CTL and their interaction is required to facilitate granule fusion.
Munc18‐1 and Munc18-2 are required for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) function, with Munc18‐ 1 required for CTL activation and Munc18 ‐2 required for CTL degranulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Munc18‐1 is not the only Munc18 family member to localize to the plasma membrane in secretory cells.
Munc18‐1 and Munc18-2 have very similar functions in the regulation of SNARE complex formation, but the localization of Munc18‐ 2 to the plasma membrane is essential for the function of STX11.
Munc18‐1 and Munc18-2 have different roles in CTL, with Munc18-1 being involved in granule biogenesis and Munc18–2 in the final steps in granule secretion.
